newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-JPN RETAILER RYOHIN TO EXPAND IN EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-JPN RETAILER RYOHIN TO EXPAND IN EUROPE.

text.p: Japanese home products retailer Ryohin Keikaku Co Ltd says it is planning to continue its expansion into Europe with new outlets in Britain, Germany and France.

"Our expansion overseas will be centred in Europe. We will increase the number of outlets in London to 10 from the current four, and we aim to set up shops in Germany and France as well," president Kaoru Ariga said in a recent interview.
"Our products appeal to mature societies because they are simple, modest and environment-friendly. We will make 'Mujirushi Ryohin' a universal brand," he added.
The Mujirushi Ryohin brand is known as "Muji" overseas, retailing home products ranging from linens and kitchenware to bicycles, food and furniture.
The company, which also has stores in Singapore and Hong Kong, operates small- and medium-sized outlets of up to 330 square metres overseas.
The company did not say when the new outlets would be established.
Ryohin Keikaku, which started as an original brand product department of Japan's fourth-largest retailer, Seiyu Ltd, is a firm specialising in original product design, both wholesale and retail.

Domestically, the company operates stores within Seiyu as well as large independent outlets in the suburbs, but Ariga said from now on Ryohin plans to concentrate on increasing selling space by establishing large outlets of more than 660 square metres each.
"We will dedicate ourselves to launching large outlets of more than 660 square metres each. The size of the shop will allow us to provide a sizable line-up of our products," Ariga said.

"Ryohin grew as a company which targeted young men and women who live on their own. As they get married and have children, however, we need more space if we want them to have our complete collection of household goods, furniture and clothing," he added.
Ariga said Ryohin intends to enlarge selling space by 264,000 square metres per year, and that it aims to strengthen product development to fill up stores 1,650 square metres big.
Sales for the first half of the 1997 business year may be slightly lower than expected due to sluggish sales of clothing after mid-May, Ariga said.
"But for the whole year, the company will be able to post a 25.6 percent year-on-year increase in parent current profit to 6.7 billion yen as planned," he said.
The company's sales for the year ending March 31, 1998, will also reach its targeted 72 billion yen, up 18.6 percent from a year earlier, he said.
